Ben — thanks, attached are our edits (redline_acme_dpa_v3.docx). A few high-level items to flag:
- Audit rights: Acme requires the right to audit annually and after material incidents; we prefer a vendor-permitted third-party auditor option.
- Subprocessors: please provide current list and SLA for subprocessors handling PHI.
- Data transfers: we need explicit confirmation on SCCs and any supplemental technical measures.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report (last 12 months) and a summary of most recent penetration test are required for procurement sign-off.

Can you confirm whether these are feasible? Procurement target is to complete legal review by 2/18.

Regards,
Elena Morales
Senior Procurement Manager — Acme Health
elena.morales@acmehealth.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodai.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodai.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Feb 2026 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: RE: DPA for signature — initial draft

Ben / Vivek — reviewed Acme's redlines. I'm listing negotiating positions so we have a unified response to Procurement: 

1) Audit rights
- Position: Accept limited audit rights to a single annual third-party SOC-style assessment, and ad-hoc audits only with a clear, material incident threshold. No unbounded site inspections.
- Compromise language option: "Customer may engage a mutually agreed independent auditor to perform a single annual audit of Vendor's controls, subject to reasonable confidentiality and disruption limits."

2) Subprocessors
- Action: Provide current subprocessors_2026.csv; commit to 30-day notice for new subprocessors and an escalation path for PHI-handling subprocessors. Any PHI processors must be SOC 2 or equivalent.

3) Data transfers / SCCs
- Position: We will rely on EU SCCs and documented technical safeguards (encryption in transit & at rest, KMS option). We can add language referencing SCCs + technical measures.

4) Evidence requests
- Deliverables: SOC 2 Type II (most recent) and a 2-page pen-test summary (redacted vendor findings). Full pen-test report reserved for reciprocal NDA or in-person review.

5) Execution path
- Send final DPA via DocuSign (we'll use envelope EX-ACME-2026-5512). Legal review before sending. If Acme insists on broader audit rights, escalate to Legal + Head of Trust for a 1:1.

I'll draft a concise reply to Acme and attach the current subprocessors list and the SOC2 stub link. Ben, please pull the SOC2 PDF and pen test summary for procurement. Vivek, confirm whether we need an exec approval for the audit clause.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwoodai.com

Attachment: subprocessors_2026.csv (csv)
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@acmehealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodai.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodai.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA for signature — initial draft

Laura / Ben,

Thanks for the clear positions. A couple quick follow-ups before legal proceeds: 
- SOC 2: procurement will accept a secured link to the SOC 2 report (redacted as necessary).
- Pen test: a 2-page executive summary is sufficient for the initial review; we will request the full report only if there are significant findings.
- Audit clause: our preference is to keep the right to a third-party audit annually; if you can accept the "mutually agreed" auditor language and confidentiality protections we can move forward.

Timeline: if we get the SOC2 link and pen-test summary by 2/12 we can keep the 2/18 legal deadline. Also please include a DocuSign envelope when you send the final DPA.

Best,
Elena
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodai.com>

Laura
